"**What Kind of Love**" is a song co-written and recorded by American country music artist Rodney Crowell. It was released in June 1992 as the second single from the album _Life Is Messy_. The song reached number 11 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart and peaked at number 2 on the _RPM_ Country Tracks in Canada.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-1)
Crowell and co-writer Will Jennings wrote the lyrics to a recording of a melody that Roy Orbison had made before his death.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-2) The song features backing vocals from Don Henley and Linda Ronstadt.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-liner-3)
Deborah Evans Price, of _Billboard_ magazine reviewed the song favorably, calling it the "first step in a major effort to immerse this rock-influenced country star into the pop and AC realm. She goes on to say that "twangy instrumentation a la Tom Petty and the late Roy Orbison (with whom this song was penned), combined with an appealing vocal, makes a strong argument for play at these and album rock formats."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-4)

"**What Kind of Love**" is a song co-written and recorded by American country music artist Rodney Crowell. It was released in June 1992 as the second single from the album _Life Is Messy_. The song reached number 11 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart and peaked at number 2 on the _RPM_ Country Tracks in Canada.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-1)
Crowell and co-writer Will Jennings wrote the lyrics to a recording of a melody that Roy Orbison had made before his death.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-2) The song features backing vocals from Don Henley and Linda Ronstadt.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-liner-3)
Deborah Evans Price, of _Billboard_ magazine reviewed the song favorably, calling it the "first step in a major effort to immerse this rock-influenced country star into the pop and AC realm. She goes on to say that "twangy instrumentation a la Tom Petty and the late Roy Orbison (with whom this song was penned), combined with an appealing vocal, makes a strong argument for play at these and album rock formats."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-4)

"**What Kind of Love**" is a song co-written and recorded by American country music artist Rodney Crowell. It was released in June 1992 as the second single from the album _Life Is Messy_. The song reached number 11 on the U.S. _Billboard_Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart and peaked at number 2 on the _RPM_ Country Tracks in Canada.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-1)
Crowell and co-writer Will Jennings wrote the lyrics to a recording of a melody that Roy Orbison had made before his death.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-2) The song features backing vocals from Don Henley and Linda Ronstadt.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-liner-3)
Deborah Evans Price, of _Billboard_ magazine reviewed the song favorably, calling it the "first step in a major effort to immerse this rock-influenced country star into the pop and AC realm. She goes on to say that "twangy instrumentation a la Tom Petty and the late Roy Orbison (with whom this song was penned), combined with an appealing vocal, makes a strong argument for play at these and album rock formats."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Kind_of_Love#cite_note-4)
